notes:
--- Quick summary ---
Lead: VP Engineering (Rohan Patel) + Head of Infrastructure (Lea Müller). Evaluation for private VPC deployment for inference platform. Primary ask: run customer-support chat + document search for regulated mortgage workflows.

Security posture: SOC2 in progress, ISO27001 targeted Q3. Absolute requirements: customer-managed KMS (rotate keys every 90 days), HSM-backed signing for audit logs, per-tenant audit logging retention 7 years, data residency for EU-sourced customers (must stay in eu-west-1 region).

Network/architecture constraints (from infra call 2026-02-18):
- No public IPs on inference nodes. Private subnets only.
- Inbound: only customer-initiated TLS via private ALB / internal NLB; control-plane callbacks must be via VPC peering or PrivateLink (customer preference: PrivateLink).
- Outbound: extremely limited egress; allow only to Redwood-managed container registry IPs, STS/KMS endpoints, and specific telemetry endpoints over TLS. All egress must go through central NAT gateway with logging.
- Routing: multi-AZ in primary region (us-east-2) with option for EU cluster for residency.
- Proxying: traffic from app-tier goes through internal LB -> inference pool. No direct internet from model servers.

Performance targets: 99th percentile latency < 120ms for short-chat calls (<=256 tokens), throughput 200 concurrent chat sessions with burst to 600. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay premium for residency/HSM but expect batching/quantization recommendations to reduce token costs.

Procurement notes: Legal wants architecture diagram showing KMS integration (customer-managed keys + Redwood control-plane access model), SLA language for private clusters, and a draft DPA with EU residency clause. Budget sign-off expected after PoC (3 months).

Quotes / paraphrase: "We cannot have secrets accessible outside our KMS scope; any caching of user input must be controllable and auditable." — Head of Infrastructure.

Suggested PoC scope: 6-week POC running document search + chat on isolated VPC in us-east-2, sample PII redaction rule set, KMS integration demo using customer key, enable audit logging to S3 (customer bucket) and show rotation/retention workflow.

Docs shared: security FAQ, minimal trusted image list, initial VPC peering checklist.

CRM shorthand / next tasks: book infra deep-dive (owner: Maya); send pre-PoC checklist to Lea; get legal confirmation on DPA template.
architecture_fit_summary:
Ceres Veil is a strong fit for Redwood Private with a few mandatory constrains: require PrivateLink or VPC Peering to control plane (no public control-plane endpoints), inference nodes in private subnets across 3 AZs in primary region (us-east-2) with optional EU replica (eu-west-1). Model servers must not have public IPs; egress only via customer NAT with full flow logs. KMS must be customer-managed; Redwood to support key usage via cross-account IAM roles or KMS grants. Audit logs to be delivered to customer S3 bucket with object lock/retention policy; optional push to SIEM via syslog collector in same VPC.

Inbound/Outbound specifics: inbound traffic originates from application tier and customer admin bastion -> internal ALB/NLB; control-plane messages from Redwood control plane will be tunneled over PrivateLink endpoints. Outbound allowed endpoints: container registry, KMS, STS, and signed telemetry endpoints; all other egress blocked.

Operational notes: recommend canary pool in dedicated subnet, autoscale policy tied to queue depth, KV cache stored on ephemeral encrypted volumes; periodic snapshotting to encrypted object store under customer key.
